key_insight: A digitally controlled converter can boost efficiency by adapting both inductance and switching frequency to the load in real time.
engineering_relevance: This enables integrated power converters to maintain higher efficiency over wide dynamic load ranges, which is valuable for on-chip power delivery and other load-varying electronics.
method: Build a reconfigurable inductor architecture with runtime-selectable effective inductance.
Use physics-based analytical models plus FEM simulations to co-optimize inductance and switching frequency.
Store optimal operating points in a lookup table and apply hysteresis control to preserve CCM during fast transients.
evidence_signal: Simulation results in the abstract report a 4.5 percentage-point gain in average efficiency and up to a 32% reduction in average power loss versus fixed configurations.
watch_item: Performance depends on sensing latency and transient behavior, so the control scheme must avoid temporary CCM violations and ensure reliable lookup-table operation.
paper_title: Adaptive Inductor and Frequency Management for Integrated Power Converters
